VIBRATION / NODAL GEOMETRY

Chladni study

Scatter grains across a quiet plate. Two modes draw a hidden geometry.

u = cos(mπx) cos(nπy) + β cos(nπx) cos(mπy)

A FEW WAYS IN

About this experiment

Drag or tap the plate to stir grains. Left/right changes m; up/down changes n. Enter stirs at the last cursor position. Space switches Sand and Nodal lines. R makes a new seeded grain arrangement. Mode mix changes the combination; Grains changes the population. P freezes grain motion while controls and stirring still work. Reduced motion starts paused with an already formed pattern. Color and PNG export remain available.

The mathematics

Two degenerate cosine modes form an idealized square nodal field on 0 ≤ x,y ≤ 1. Mode indices count half-waves; the mix β changes their relative weight. Contours trace u = 0. The grains move toward those zeros by geometric relaxation using the analytic gradient. They are a visual guide, not a mechanical sand simulation or a full elastic-plate solver, and no sound is produced. Equal indices with β = −1 cancel everywhere, so no unique nodal lines remain. Changing a mode reforms the grains; stirring disturbs only a local patch.
